fatal_errors: The proposed Hf-to-Al substitution does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr to form approximately 4 vol.% reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase.

The cited evidence concerns a different Al-containing alloy in which the inverted BCC/B2 microstructure was produced by solution treatment and prolonged annealing; it does not establish that Al substitution in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will generate the claimed morphology.
The evidence only reports mechanical testing up to 600 °C and therefore does not support retention of approximately 855 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses the stated engineering objective and proposes a controlled composition series, matched baseline, explicit compression conditions, and quantitative rejection thresholds. It is therefore testable and scientifically plausible as an alternative. However, it misses the target composition, secondary-phase identity and morphology, and dual strengthening/toughening mechanism. The target uses dilute Cr addition to produce a reticulated Laves network, lattice contraction, and simultaneous increases in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain; the generated hypothesis instead predicts discrete B2 precipitates after substantial Hf replacement and only strength retention. Its baseline density also differs from the hidden baseline, and it omits the baseline fracture strain. Most importantly, the sole citation supports processing-induced phase inversion in another alloy rather than the claimed response of HfMoTaTiZr to Al substitution or its performance at 1000 °C. The proposed experiment is nevertheless reasonably discriminating because it includes an x=0 control, phase characterization, density measurements, two-temperature mechanical tests, and numerical failure criteria.
